title: island-free
about:
- Run the dead-end check algorithm
- Drop every vessel shorter than 45 µm, one typical capillary segment
  - that touches no junction at either end

title: dead-end check
about:
- Run the bridges algorithm
- For each vessel with an open end, shorter than ten widths
  - drop it when its ridge is under half the field's typical vessel's
  - and it beats its own quarter-turned copy by under 35% of the typical vessel's lead

title: bridges
about:
- Run the repair algorithm
- From each open end away from the frame, follow the cheapest path along the ridges of the signal
  - up to twelve widths ahead, within 60° of the way the vessel ran
  - to land on another vessel or another open end
- Keep the path as a vessel
  - when its dimmest stretch keeps 40% of the two vessels' contrast
  - it arrives at about the same depth
  - and it closes no short loop

title: repair
about:
- Run the skeleton algorithm, first filling every hole in the mark narrower than a vessel (a dim lumen)
- Move each curve point onto the brightest line across its vessel
- Drop a low-confidence vessel that is a speck, not a line
  - its signal must beat the same curve turned a quarter turn
  - and it may wander no more than a capillary does
- Break each short loop at its weakest vessel, unless that one is as strong as a typical vessel
- Bridge each gap: an open end facing another end or a vessel's side a few widths ahead, at the same depth
  - only when the gap between them carries signal
- Split a four-way junction whose arms pair into two straight lines at different depths: two vessels crossing
